title: Saudi Arabia is getting dragged into a war it has tried desperately to avoid
facts: Saudi Arabian fighter jets and US planes carried out joint military strikes across eastern Iraq.
China mediated a diplomatic agreement between Saudi Arabia and Iran in 2023.
Houthi forces launched missiles targeting two Saudi oil complexes on the Red Sea coast.
Satellite imagery indicated extensive damage to a Saudi oil facility at Jazan near the Yemeni border.
The Houthis announced a maritime blockade of Saudi shipping transiting the Bab al-Mandeb strait.
Saudi Arabia plans to expand oil exports through the Red Sea to roughly 9 million barrels per day over three years.
Saudi Arabia launched a military offensive against Houthi forces in northern Yemen in 2015.
A truce between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis was established in 2022.
Nawaf Obeid works in the Department of War Studies at King's College London.
The Saudi air force conducted retaliatory strikes against the Houthi-controlled port of Hodeidah.
Pro-Iranian militias in southern Iraq launched drone barrages targeting critical infrastructure and Riyadh.
US Central Command reported over 30 drone attacks directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.
A 2019 drone and missile attack on the Abqaiq refinery disabled nearly half of Saudi Arabia's oil production.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Riyadh to offer an integrated air defense system against Iranian drones.
Saudi Arabia recorded its largest quarterly budget deficit since 2018 in the first quarter of the year.
